en.title: GTA 6 Shatters Records With Massive Physical Launch, No Disc Required
en.summary: Despite launching without a physical disc, Grand Theft Auto VI has achieved the biggest physical game launch of the decade in several key markets. The game's boxed editions, containing only a download code, have driven unprecedented sales figures across the UK, France, and Spain.
en.body:
The hype surrounding **Grand Theft Auto VI** is undeniable, but its recent launch has presented a fascinating paradox: it's the biggest physical game release of the decade, even though it doesn't actually contain a disc.

Players purchasing a physical copy of **GTA 6** will receive a box containing a download code, a move that aligns with the industry's broader shift towards digital distribution. Yet, this absence of a physical disc has done little to dampen enthusiasm. In the UK, **GTA 6** generated approximately 32 million GBP from physical sales at launch, surpassing every other title released in the 2020s and marking the best physical game sales since 2019's **FIFA 20**. The situation is similar in France, where over one million boxed copies were sold within the first three days, a performance remarkably close to that of **GTA 5** over a decade ago. In Spain, the physical launch of **GTA 6** has been recorded as the biggest since sales tracking began.

## Retail Resurgence Amidst Digital Dominance

This impressive physical performance, despite the lack of a disc, suggests that the traditional boxed product still holds a powerful allure for consumers. It appears **Rockstar Games** has managed to capitalize on the demand for physical editions – the perceived value, the collectible aspect, the ability to display it on a shelf – while sidestepping the associated manufacturing and distribution costs of physical media. This strategy is particularly noteworthy given that physical copies still represent a significant portion of sales for current-generation consoles, with Sony's own first-party PS5 titles seeing as much as 33 percent of shipped copies being discs. The decision by **Rockstar** and **Sony** to push towards an all-digital future, even to the point of having empty disc space in **GTA 6**'s box, could indeed have a lasting impact on how AAA games are released going forward.

## Fan Reactions and Future Implications

The move away from physical discs has, understandably, sparked debate among fans. While many appreciate the convenience of digital downloads and the ability to pre-load games, others lament the loss of tangible ownership and the potential for resale. Some discussions online have pointed to the possibility of a physical disc version being released later, perhaps in December 2026, as a measure to prevent leaks, though details on such a release have not yet been officially confirmed.

## What's Next

As **GTA 6** continues its record-breaking sales trajectory, all eyes will be on how other major developers and publishers respond to this trend. The success of **GTA 6**'s disc-less physical launch might just be the catalyst that accelerates the complete transition to digital for the gaming industry.

content_raw: As announced this year, GTA 6 came out with no disc to boot, and even if you did buy it at a retail store, you’d just get a code. What’s funny is there is space for the disc in the box itself, but it is tragically empty amid Sony and Rockstar’s push toward an all-digital future. However, even though it has no disc at all, GTA 6 is one of the biggest physical launches of the decade, and in some countries it’s the definitive number one. According to The Game Business , GTA 6 generated around 32 million GBP from physical sales at launch in the UK, beating every single title of the 2020s and becoming the best-selling physical game since 2019’s FIFA 20 . In France, the game apparently sold over a million physical copies in its first three days, which The Game Business says is very close to how GTA 5 performed 13 years ago. In Spain, GTA 6 ‘s physical launch is the biggest since sales tracking began. Image via Rockstar Games Make sure you go and check out our sister site, GTA 6 Bible , for all your GTA 6 needs. As such, Rockstar seems to have reaped all the benefits of physical media but saved itself the costs and the trouble of printing out millions of discs that’d let consumers actually own what they had purchased. In line with Sony’s decision to kill discs off completely in 2028, Rockstar’s decision could have a lasting, if not permanent, impact on the future of physical editions, as many AAA studios will doubtless begin following in its footsteps. Physical copies still account for a large portion of total sales for PS5 games, with Sony’s own first-party titles seeing as much as 33 percent of total copies shipped being discs. Digital is naturally the more popular and significantly more accessible option, but discs nevertheless sell rather well and generate way more revenue than Sony or others would like you to believe, especially when it comes to singleplayer games. Imagine just how many more Rockstar may have sold if people actually got a disc with their box and had a real reason to go physical, beyond a poster or whatever other goodies the company decided to include as a “bonus” to make up for the lack of the only thing that gives physical editions any meaning.
